title: BATS seasonal effects do not explain A22 AOU changes near Bermuda on density 26.5 under a shared-cycle assumption
abstract: We tested whether different sampling seasons explain the large A22 apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) changes near Bermuda that a decade-forced ventilation model missed. We fitted year and calendar-month effects to 399 BATS year-month means from 1989-2025 and transferred the month effects to paired A22 bins at 28-36 N on potential-density anomaly 26.5 kg/m3. The seasonal effects are -0.47, -0.53 and -0.59 micromol/kg for 1997-2003, 2003-2012 and 2012-2021. The observed changes are +12.94, -12.89 and +20.87. After adjustment they are +13.41, -12.36 and +21.46. Narrower latitude ranges, strict interpolation, split-period seasonal fits and exclusion of occupation years retain the large changes. A seasonal correction also leaves most of the large depth changes after 2003 in place. Thus a mean seasonal sampling correction does not resolve the model error near Bermuda. The main assumption is that the BATS cycle applies to A22. Spatial transfer error, correlated section bins and calibration errors are not included in the reported conditional bootstrap intervals. This test does not identify the cause of the remaining changes.

display.caption: BATS calendar-month AOU effects after year means are removed, A22 changes before and after seasonal adjustment, and BATS annual means. Intervals are conditional on transferring the BATS cycle to A22.

citations.reason: We test whether seasonal sampling explains the large section changes missed by this model.
We reuse its BATS extraction code under its baseline MIT terms.
We use its GLODAP line-bin aggregate table.
Its annual forcing correction motivates a separate check for seasonal sampling error.
